definitions.meaning: describes a figure nipped in sharply at the waist
a sand-glass, the old-fashioned device for measuring time

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow-waisted figure is called this shape, and the sand-filled glass is an antique device for timing.

indicators.note: topless says the first letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: gowns are long robes

explanation.surface: A risque wardrobe item: someone has robes that leave the top bare.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of the next word are made into a new form

explanation.surface: A fashion feature printed in a magazine for reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' rearranges ARTICLE. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a reading of poetry is one kind of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A public reading of poems or texts is a kind of performance given to an audience.

clue.text: An oil distributed between ends of Lincoln, perhaps

definitions.text: An oil distributed between ends of Lincoln, perhaps

indicators.note: between says the rearranged letters sit inside the other piece
ends of picks the first and last letters of the city name
distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An oil spread around the edges of Lincoln, perhaps in its wool trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges AN OIL into ANOLI, which goes 'between' L and N, the 'ends of' Lincoln. Lincoln was a wool town, and this grease comes from sheep's wool, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The greasy substance from sheep's wool is used as an oily base for ointments.

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a riot or noisy commotion is a scene, as in 'make a scene'

explanation.surface: A news report of a riot that someone saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' takes SCENE (a fuss or commotion) by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something observed with one's own eyes has been seen.

clue.text: How apprehensively we regard condensation and corrosion? Comprehensively!

parts.note: mist is fine water droplets condensed in the air
rust is corrosion of iron
fully means completely or comprehensively

explanation.surface: A homeowner eyeing damp and rust with deep suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How ... we regard' frames the definition: apprehensively is the way we regard damp and corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarding something with suspicion and doubt is to do so apprehensively.

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, used in British slang
an order to pelt crows with rocks, corvine meaning of crows and lapidation meaning stoning

explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation of astonishment literally reads as a command to throw rocks at rooks and ravens.

clue.text: The Emperor, or a conception of it we hear

indicators.note: what we hear of it is one rendering, so the letters are rendered in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Musing on Beethoven's Emperor, or an interpretation of it heard in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emperor is the nickname of Beethoven's fifth work in this form. The letters of OR A CONCEPTION are reordered: 'of it we hear' suggests a performance or interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Fifth for keyboard and orchestra is nicknamed the Emperor.

clue.text: She is one going to church, express

parts.note: she is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman on her way to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She is one' is not a woman: 'she' is a grammatical part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce a verdict or opinion is to state it, to express it formally.

clue.text: Great show of antiquity in butler's room

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pantry is the butler's room in a grand house
age means antiquity, great oldness

explanation.surface: A grand display of old silver in the butler's room.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid ceremonial display or spectacle is what makes a great show.

clue.text: The custom is lawful, people say

indicators.note: people say signals the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: something right is just and lawful

explanation.surface: A remark that a tradition is legally allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial custom or ritual practice.

clue.text: A cost in lives from Bikini, possibly?

parts.note: the death toll is the cost in lives

explanation.surface: The deaths caused by a skimpy swimsuit, or by nuclear tests at Bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is not the swimsuit but the Pacific island where nuclear bombs were tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a coral reef island ring in the Marshall Islands, an example of this formation.

definitions.meaning: a former coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee
the heroine of The King and I, governess to the King of Siam's children

explanation.definitionFit: An old Indian coin shares its name with Leonowens, the English tutor at the Siamese court.

clue.text: Deposit, for example, held by doctors

indicators.note: held by says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors

explanation.definitionFit: Sediment at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit.

definitions.meaning: reprimanded, called in for a telling-off

explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a scold, and to rebuke someone is to give them a telling-off.

definitions.meaning: Switzerland is the classic country that stays out of wars

explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means taking no side, and Switzerland is famous for staying out of wars between nations.

parts.note: a hanging was grimly called a 'party' of this kind; the noose put an end to the guest of honour

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a hanging was a party named after this neckwear, with the rope as the tie.

definitions.meaning: read as two words: up, out of bed, and tight, slang for drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and inhibited is the sense; split in two it reads as awake yet still drunk.

clue.text: Criterion, perhaps, for the rate of exchange

indicators.note: exchange means swap around, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A standard used for the rate of currency exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The Criterion is a playhouse in London's Piccadilly Circus; 'rate of exchange' looks like finance but 'exchange' rearranges THE RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Criterion is a famous London playhouse, an example of a venue for drama.

clue.text: Vessel gone at sea, with every, body aboard

indicators.note: aboard says one piece is put inside the other
at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A ship lost at sea with everyone on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges GONE into GEON, and ALL goes 'aboard' it. The comma in 'every, body' is probably a print slip for 'everybody'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large old Spanish sailing ship is a vessel.

clue.text: Well-bred gentleman, rather short, has general reversal

indicators.note: rather short says the word is heavily cut, keeping only its start
reversal says the general's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A short gentleman with a general's habit of turning back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather short' cuts gentleman to GENT; 'reversal' turns LEE into EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined and polite, of good breeding.

clue.text: Union strike? It is on the cards!

definitions.meaning: a society or association of members
to hit with a heavy stick
one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: A society, a heavy stick used to hit, and one of the four card suits.
To signify or have in mind, and also wealth or income.

parts.note: in Joel Chandler Harris's tales of Uncle Remus, the dialect word placed before Rabbit and Fox

explanation.definitionFit: The Southern dialect form used for 'brother' in the folk tales told by Uncle Remus.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story, the stuff of legend and folklore.

indicators.note: endless says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a block is a jam or obstruction

explanation.surface: A coalition stuck in a traffic jam that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nations or parties joined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Only Welsh capt, to convert, sends it up

indicators.note: to convert means to change, so the letters are rearranged; also a rugby pun on kicking a conversion

explanation.surface: A rugby captain from Wales takes the conversion kick himself and boots it high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to convert' rearranges ONLY WELSH CAPT. The surface is rugby: a conversion kick sends the ball up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool around or mock something for laughs is to send it up.

parts.note: not the railway buffers at the end of a track, but a person at a station who polishes travellers' footwear

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who polishes footwear for a living, often at a railway terminus, is a bootblack.
